en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One more question along these lines and then I want to zoom out on just where AI is heading and something I love to ask folks like you that are at the cutting edge of AI is what you're teaching your kids.
zh: 关于这方面还有一个问题，然后我想把视角拉大到 AI 的发展方向，我喜欢问像你这样处于 AI 前沿的人的一个问题是，你在教你的孩子什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you have kids, I feel like the world is going to be very different when they grow up.
zh: 我知道你有孩子，我觉得当他们长大时，世界将会非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you encouraging them to learn that you think is different maybe from previous generations to help them be successful in a world of AI abundance?
zh: 你在鼓励他们学习什么？你认为这可能与前几代人不同，以帮助他们在 AI 丰富的世界中取得成功？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if I'm teaching them differently, but I'm really trying to encourage them to make AI a part of their lives.
zh: 我不知道我是否在教他们不同的东西，但我真的在鼓励他们让 AI 成为他们生活的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was reflecting actually when I took the AP calculus exams in '97, '98 AB and BC, I could use a graphing calculator.
zh: 我实际上在回想，当我在 97、98 年参加 AP 微积分考试（AB 和 BC）时，我可以使用图形计算器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I haven't done this research I was meaning to plug this into ChatGPT before our conversation, but I'll do it after.
zh: 我还没有做过这项研究，我本打算在我们谈话前把这个输入到 ChatGPT 中，但我会在之后做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did the calculus exam change before and after they allowed the calculator in the exam?
zh: 在考试允许使用计算器之前和之后，微积分考试有发生变化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I assume it did.
zh: 我假设它变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But essentially, to when you allow the calculator in the exam, you need to make sure that none of the questions benefit people for having a calculator or not, which actually forces you to rethink the problems to test calculus knowledge that don't benefit from like road arithmetic or the other things you can do on a graphing calculator.
zh: 但本质上，当你在考试中允许使用计算器时，你需要确保没有任何题目会因为拥有计算器或不拥有计算器而获益，这实际上迫使你重新思考问题，以测试不依赖于基础算术或你在图形计算器上可以做的其他事情的微积分知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that a lot of education doesn't presume you have a super intelligence in your pocket.
zh: 我认为很多教育并不预设你口袋里有一个超级智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, if you ask someone to write an essay on a book that they read, you could probably hallucinate one pretty easily from one of the big providers like ChatGPT.
zh: 所以，如果你要求某人写一篇关于他们读过的书的文章，你很可能很容易从像 ChatGPT 这样的大型提供商那里产生幻觉得到一篇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe if you are skilled enough that prompting, maybe even your teacher won't know it's written by an AI.
zh: 也许如果你足够熟练于提示词，甚至你的老师都不会知道这是 AI 写的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what do you do?
zh: 那你该怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you teach kids differently?
zh: 你如何以不同的方式教孩子？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard for teachers right now because I think we haven't gone through the transition of adding calculators to the exams.
zh: 这对老师来说真的很难，因为我认为我们还没有经历在考试中添加计算器的过渡期。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think a lot of the mechanisms we have to evaluate students are broken by the existence of ChatGPT and the like.
zh: 所以，我认为我们用来评估学生的许多机制被 ChatGPT 等事物的存在打破了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're in a very awkward phase, but I think we can still both teach kids how to think and teach kids how to learn.
zh: 所以我认为我们处于一个非常尴尬的阶段，但我认为我们仍然可以既教孩子如何思考，又教孩子如何学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think our education system can catch up and I actually think these models can be one of the most effective educational tools in history.
zh: 我认为我们的教育体系能够赶上，我实际上认为这些模型可能是历史上最有效的教育工具之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if you're a visual learner or reading learner.
zh: 我不知道你是否是视觉学习者或阅读学习者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to read.
zh: 我喜欢阅读。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't love going to lectures.
zh: 我不喜欢去听讲座。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't learn that well from them.
zh: 我从讲座中学得不是很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to read the book and if you have a teacher who doesn't teach in your style, you can now go home and ask ChatGPT to teach you in another mechanism.
zh: 我喜欢读这本书，如果你有一位不以你的风格教学的老师，你现在可以回家让 ChatGPT 用另一种机制来教你。

speaker: Unknown
en: My kids use ChatGPT to quiz them before a test.
zh: 我的孩子在考试前使用 ChatGPT 向他们提问。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can use audio mode or chat mode.
zh: 你可以使用音频模式或聊天模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's better than cue cards.
zh: 这比抽认卡更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: My daughter took home a Shakespeare book, she took a picture of a page she didn't understand and ChatGPT explained it to her way better than I would've as well.
zh: 我女儿带了一本莎士比亚的书回家，她拍了一张她看不懂的页面的照片，ChatGPT 向她解释的方式比我解释得要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every child in this world has a personalized tutor that can teach them in the way that they best learn, visually, over audio, reading.
zh: 我认为这个世界上的每个孩子都有一位个性化导师，可以以他们最擅长的方式，无论是视觉上、通过音频还是阅读，来教他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a platform that can test you, that can quiz you.
zh: 我们有一个可以测试你、可以向你提问的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really an amplifier of agency.
zh: 我认为它真的是主观能动性的放大器。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the kids who have agency, who have aspirations to learn something, I think you have what is the best combination of every teacher you've ever had and these models and you can use it.
zh: 我认为那些具有主观能动性、有学习愿望的孩子，我认为你拥有你曾经拥有的每一位老师的最佳组合和这些模型，你可以使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with my kids, my oldest daughter learned how to code and she was making a website and every time she had a question for me, I would just make her use ChatGPT.
zh: 对我的孩子们来说，我的大女儿学会了写代码，她在做一个网站，每次她问我问题，我就让她用 ChatGPT。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not because I was trying to be an obnoxious father, but I'm like she needs to learn to use this tool because it's amazing.
zh: 不是因为我试图做一个烦人的父亲，而是我觉得她需要学会使用这个工具，因为它很神奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I really am trying to have them learn how to use it constructively in their lives.
zh: 所以，我真的在试图让他们学会如何在生活中建设性地使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But all that said, I just feel a ton of empathy for public school teachers right now.
zh: 但尽管如此，我现在对公立学校的老师充满同情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard because the technology is moving faster than our educational system.
zh: 这非常困难，因为技术发展比我们的教育体系更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think particularly as it relates to evaluation, it's just really challenging for teachers right now.
zh: 我认为特别是在评估方面，这对老师来说真的很有挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I worry because these technologies amplify agency, the opposite can also be true.
zh: 我担心是因为这些技术增强了主观能动性，反之亦然。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are a student trying to not learn something, I think these tools probably provide a lot of mechanisms to avoid it as well.
zh: 如果你是一个试图不想学习的学生，我认为这些工具可能也提供了很多机制来逃避学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I think there's a challenge for parents and teachers and I think we're going to end up with a handful of years here.
zh: 所以，我认为这对父母和老师来说都是一个挑战，我认为我们会有几年的时间在这里度过。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I brought up the calculus AP exam because obviously, a graphing calculator is not ChatGPT, don't get me wrong.
zh: 但我提到微积分 AP 考试是因为，显然，图形计算器不是 ChatGPT，别误会我的意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we've been able to figure out a way to conform homework and in-class learning and tests around the technologies available to us fairly successfully to date.
zh: 但我认为我们已经能够找到一种方法，围绕我们可以获得的技术来调整家庭作业、课堂学习和考试，到目前为止相当成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm fairly confident we'll figure it out and I think it's going to... And on the much more positive side, I don't know, I went to public schools, I don't know if you did too.
zh: 我相当确信我们会搞定它，我认为这将会……在更积极的一面，我不知道，我上的是公立学校，我不知道你是不是也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: You end up with some pretty bad teachers at times and now, you have an outlet.
zh: 你有时会遇到一些相当糟糕的老师，而现在，你有了一个出口。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need to be the rich kid who can afford a tutor anymore to get tutoring.
zh: 你不需要是那个请得起家教的富家子弟才能获得辅导。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are a kid who excels in math and your school doesn't have advanced statistics classes, well, now you do.
zh: 如果你是一个擅长数学的孩子，而你的学校没有高级统计课程，那么现在你有了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think this is just an incredibly democratizing force with kids who have agency and I think that's very exciting.
zh: 所以我认为这对拥有主观能动性的孩子来说是一种不可思议的民主化力量，我认为这非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm hopeful that there's a 11-year-old right now who's going to start a really amazing company 10 years from now whose ChatGPT is going to be their primary tutor that led to that outcome.
zh: 我希望现在有一个 11 岁的孩子，将在 10 年后创办一家非常棒的公司，其 ChatGPT 将是促成这一结果的主要导师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's pretty cool.
zh: 我认为这很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a two-year-old and it feels like there's a new milestone of, there's like when to give them a phone, when to give them, I don't know, Snapchat, whatever kids use these days and then it's like when to give them their first ChatGPT account.
zh: 我有一个两岁的孩子，感觉就像有一个新的里程碑，比如什么时候给他们手机，什么时候给他们，我不知道，Snapchat，不管现在的孩子们用什么，然后就是什么时候给他们第一个 ChatGPT 账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well no, I wonder how soon that's supposed to happen.
zh: 不，我想知道这应该发生得有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my personal take is, it's different than the former two.
zh: 我认为我个人的看法是，这与前两者不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think mobile phones are great in school or great for kids and I personally advocate for waiting a long time.
zh: 我认为手机在学校或对孩子来说都不是什么好事，我个人主张要等待很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that ChatGPT is more like Google search and it's one thing to have a device in your pocket that's addictive and has push notifications, but it's another thing to use AI to learn.
zh: 但我认为 ChatGPT 更像 Google 搜索，口袋里有一个有成瘾性并且有推送通知的设备是一回事，但使用人工智能来学习是另一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I think the two are different.
zh: 所以，我认为这两者是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really think of AI fundamentally as a utility.
zh: 我真的认为人工智能从根本上说是一种公用设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think a lot of parents before ChatGPT said, "When should I let my kid use Google search?"
zh: 我认为很多父母在 ChatGPT 出现之前并没有说，“我什么时候应该让我的孩子使用 Google 搜索？”

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a different type of tool.
zh: 那是一种不同类型的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think thinking of it like that is the way I think about these technologies.
zh: 我认为这样思考是我看待这些技术的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the form factor for your kids like an iPad or a laptop or something?
zh: 你的孩子们的设备形态像 iPad 还是笔记本电脑之类的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They use the computer on the desk.
zh: 他们用书桌上的电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got it.
zh: 明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good tips.
zh: 好建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is good for me to learn all these things as my kid ages.
zh: 随着我的孩子长大，学习这些东西对我来说很有好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I'm going to zoom out and let's talk about business strategy AI.
zh: 好的，我将 zoom out（拉远视角），让我们来谈谈商业策略 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the biggest questions a lot of founders think about these days is just where should I build?
zh: 如今许多创始人思考的最大问题之一就是，我该在哪里构建？

speaker: Unknown
en: What will foundational model companies not squash and do themselves?
zh: 基础模型公司不会挤压并自己做哪些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Being someone building a very successful AI business and also being on the board of OpenAI, feel like you have a really unique perspective on what is probably a good idea and it's probably not a good idea.
zh: 作为一名正在构建非常成功的 AI 业务的人，同时也是 OpenAI 的董事会成员，我觉得你对什么可能是个好主意以及什么可能不是好主意有着非常独特的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think the AI market is going to play out and where do you think founders should focus and also just try to avoid?
zh: 你认为 AI 市场将如何发展，你认为创始人应该关注哪里以及应该尝试避免什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's three segments of the AI market that will end up fairly meaningful markets and then I'll end with how I think it's going to play out.
zh: 我认为 AI 市场有三个细分市场最终会成为相当重要的市场，然后我将结束我认为它会如何发展的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first is the frontier model market or foundation model market.
zh: 首先是前沿模型市场或基础模型市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this will end up the small handful of hyperscalers and really big labs just like the cloud infrastructure as a service market.
zh: 我认为这将最终变成少数几个超大规模的云服务商和真正的大型实验室，就像云基础设施即服务市场一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is that creating a frontier model is entirely a function of CapEx.
zh: 原因在于创建前沿模型完全是资本支出的函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need a company with huge amounts of CapEx capacity to build one of these models.
zh: 你需要一家拥有巨大资本支出能力的公司来构建这些模型中的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of the companies that were startups that tried to do this have already been consolidated or almost all of them, inflection, adapt, character and others.
zh: 所有尝试这样做的初创公司都已经被整合了，或者几乎所有的，inflection、adapt、character 和其他公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there doesn't appear to be a viable business model for a startup because of the amount of CapEx required and there's just not enough fundraising runway to get to escape velocity.
zh: 我认为对于初创公司来说，似乎没有可行的商业模式，因为所需的资本支出量很大，而且没有足够的筹资跑道来达到逃逸速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, the models deteriorate in value fairly quickly as an asset class.
zh: 而且，作为一种资产类别，模型的价值下降得相当快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you need just a lot of scale to make a return on the investment for a model that deteriorates in value so quickly.
zh: 所以，你需要大量的规模才能为价值下降如此之快的模型获得投资回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I think that's going to end up probably no entrepreneur should build a frontier model.
zh: 所以，我认为最终可能没有企业家应该构建前沿模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's my take.
zh: 那就是我的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unless you're Elon.
zh: 除非你是 Elon。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah.
zh: 噢，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's different.
zh: 他是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he has the capacity to raise billions in capital and my guess is most of your other listeners don't, and then he is the greatest of all time for reason and he's different.
zh: 他有能力筹集数十亿美元的资本，我猜你其他的大多数听众都没有，而且他是有史以来最伟大的，这是有原因的，他是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't compare yourself to him.
zh: 你不要拿自己和他比。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other part of the market is the tooling, and I think there's a lot of folks selling pickaxes in the Gold Rush.
zh: 市场的另一部分是工具，我想很多人都在淘金热中卖铲子。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is data labeling, services.
zh: 这是数据标注，服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is data platforms, it's eval tools.
zh: 这是数据平台，它是评估工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: More specialized models like 11 Labs has a great set of voice models that a lot of companies use that are really high quality and it's like if you're trying to be successful in AI, what are the different tools and services that you need?
zh: 更专门的模型，比如 11 Labs 有一套很棒的语音模型，很多公司都在用，质量真的很高，就像如果你想在 AI 方面取得成功，你需要哪些不同的工具和服务？

speaker: Unknown
en: There is some risk to the tooling market because it's pretty close to the sun.
zh: 工具市场存在一些风险，因为它离太阳很近。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, if you look at the infrastructure as a service market and the cloud tooling market like the Confluent and Databricks and Snowflake, a lot of the Amazon and Azure and others have competing products in those areas because they're very adjacent to the infrastructure itself and every infrastructure provider is trying to differentiate by moving up the stack and you're right there.
zh: 所以，如果你看看基础设施即服务市场和云工具市场，像 Confluent、Databricks 和 Snowflake，很多 Amazon 和 Azure 以及其他人在这些领域都有竞争产品，因为它们与基础设施本身非常接近，每个基础设施提供商都在试图通过向技术栈上层移动来实现差异化，而你就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, there's some real meaningful companies as I mentioned, like Snowflake, Databricks, Confluent and others, but there's a lot of others that were obviated by technology from the infrastructure providers themselves.
zh: 所以，正如我提到的，有一些真正有意义的公司，比如 Snowflake、Databricks、Conflent 和其他公司，但还有很多其他公司被基础设施提供商本身的技术淘汰了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those companies probably are the most at risk for a developer day from one of these big foundation model companies releasing exactly what they do.
zh: 所以这些公司可能是风险最高的，因为如果这些大型基础模型公司中的一家在某一天发布了他们所做的确切东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's probably a lot of people who need your tool, but the question will be if or when is probably the right way to think about it, one of these large infrastructure providers introduces a competitor, why will people continue to choose you?
zh: 所以可能很多人需要你的工具，但问题会是，如果或者何时可能是思考它的正确方式，这些大型基础设施提供商中的一家引入了竞争对手，为什么人们会继续选择你？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a good market but it's a little bit close to the end as I said.
zh: 所以这是一个好市场，但正如我所说，它有点接近终点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then there's the applied AI market.
zh: 然后还有应用 AI 市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this will play out for companies who build agents.
zh: 我认为这将对构建智能体的公司发挥作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think agent is the new app.
zh: 我认为智能体是新的应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's going to be the product form factor.
zh: 我认为这将是产品形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's companies like Sierra, we help companies build agents to answer the phone or answer the chat for customer experience and customer service.
zh: 有像 Sierra 这样的公司，我们帮助公司构建智能体来接听电话或回答聊天，以提供客户体验和客户服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's companies like Harvey that make agents for both a legal, paralegal profession, anti-trust reviews, reviewing contracts etc, etc.
zh: 有像 Harvey 这样的公司，它们为法律、律师助理行业、反垄断审查、审查合同等制作智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's companies that do content marketing.
zh: 有做内容营销的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's companies that do supply chain analysis.
zh: 有做供应链分析的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is like the software as a service market.
zh: 我认为这就像软件即服务市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll probably be higher margin companies because you're selling something that achieves a business outcome as opposed to being a byproduct of the models themselves.
zh: 它们可能是利润率更高的公司，因为你销售的是能实现业务成果的东西，而不是模型本身的副产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will almost certainly pay taxes down to the model providers, which is why those model providers will end up extremely large scale but probably slightly lower margin and I think the market for them will be probably less technical.
zh: 它们几乎肯定会向模型提供商纳税，这就是为什么那些模型提供商最终将达到极大的规模，但利润率可能会略低，我认为它们的市场技术性可能会更低。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the purest form of software as a service, it's not like you ask what database do you use?
zh: 如果你想一想软件即服务的最纯粹形式，并不是像你问你使用什么数据库？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really about the feature and function.
zh: 它真的是关于特性和功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's where agents will go.
zh: 我认为这就是智能体的发展方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's going to be more about product than it is about technology over time.
zh: 我认为随着时间的推移，更多的是关于产品，而不是关于技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just going back to my metaphor, in 1998 when Mark and Parker started Salesforce, just getting that database running in the cloud was like a technical achievement.
zh: 回到我的比喻，1998 年当 Mark 和 Parker 创办 Salesforce 时，仅仅让那个数据库在云上运行就像是一个技术成就。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nowadays, no one asks about that because you can just spin up a database in AWS or Azure and it's like no problem.
zh: 如今，没人问那个，因为你可以在 AWS 或 Azure 中直接启动一个数据库，这就像没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think today, orchestrating an agentic process on top of the models, sounds really fancy and it's really hard and all that stuff.
zh: 我认为今天，在模型之上编排一个智能体流程，听起来真的很花哨，也真的很难，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm pretty sure that's going to be easy in three or four years.
zh: 我很确定这在三四年后会变得很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like just as the technology improves.
zh: 就像随着技术的改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, over time you say, what is an agent company?
zh: 所以，随着时间的推移，你会说，什么是智能体公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it looks a little bit like [inaudible 00:57:30] as a service.
zh: 嗯，它看起来有点像 [听不清 00:57:30] 即服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: You talk a little bit less about how you deal with the models in the same way modern SaaS, few people ask what database you use, but you'll probably ask a lot about the workflows and what business outcomes that you're driving.
zh: 你会少谈论一些你如何处理模型，就像现代 SaaS，很少有人问你使用什么数据库，但你可能会问很多关于工作流和你正在推动的业务成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you generating leads for a sales team?
zh: 你是在为销售团队挖掘潜在客户吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you minimizing your procurement spend?
zh: 你是在最小化你的采购支出吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever value you're providing, it's going to slowly evolve towards that.
zh: 无论你提供什么价值，它都会慢慢地向那个方向演变。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm very excited.
zh: 我非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think startups should probably build foundation models.
zh: 我不认为初创公司应该构建基础模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can shoot your shot if you have a vision for the future, go for it.
zh: 但如果你对未来的愿景有想法，你可以试一试，去追求它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's probably a challenging market that's already consolidated.
zh: 但我认为这可能是一个充满挑战的市场，而且已经整合了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm very excited about the other two markets.
zh: 我对另外两个市场感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm particularly excited as building agents becomes easier, to see a lot of long tail agent companies come out.
zh: 我特别兴奋的是，随着构建智能体变得更容易，看到很多长尾智能体公司出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was looking at a website for the top 50 software companies in the stock market and obviously, the top five are the big, big boom ones like Microsoft, Amazon, Google, all that, but the next 50 are all SaaS companies and some of them are very exciting, some of them are super boring, but this is how the software market has evolved and I think we're going to see something similar with agents.
zh: 我在看一个股市前 50 大软件公司的网站，显然，前五名是那些大的、大的繁荣公司，比如 Microsoft、Amazon、Google 等等，但接下来的 50 家都是 SaaS 公司，其中一些非常令人兴奋，一些超级无聊，但这就是软件市场的演变方式，我认为我们将看到智能体有类似的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just going to be these huge markets like we're in customer service and software engineering.
zh: 这不仅仅会是我们处于客户服务和软件工程中的这些巨大市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be a lot of things where people are spending a lot of time and resources that an agent can just solve, but it requires an entrepreneur who actually understands that business problem, and deeply, and I think that's where a lot of the value is going to be unlocked in the AI market.
zh: 它将会有很多事情，人们在这些事情上花费大量时间和资源，而智能体可以直接解决，但这需要一位真正理解该业务问题的企业家，并且理解得很深刻，我认为这就是 AI 市场中大量价值将被解锁的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is incredibly helpful.
zh: 这非常有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: This makes me think about, I had Marc Benioff on the podcast, you guys were co-CEOs and he was extremely agent-pilled.
zh: 这让我想起，我请 Marc Benioff 上过播客，你们曾是联席 CEO，而且他对智能体非常着迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: All he wanted to talk about was Agentforce.
zh: 他只想谈论 Agentforce。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly you're also very agent-pilled.
zh: 显然你也非常 agent-pilled（沉迷智能体）。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it that-
zh: 是什么让人——

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never heard the term agent-pilled [inaudible 00:59:18].
zh: 我从未听说过 agent-pilled 这个词 [听不清 00:59:18]。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly you guys saw something that was just like, okay, we need to go all in on agents.
zh: 显然你们看到了某种东西，就像是，好吧，我们需要全力以赴投入智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the future.
zh: 这就是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it you think people are missing about just why this is such a critical change in the way software is going to work?
zh: 你认为人们关于为什么这是软件工作方式如此关键的变化这一点上，错过了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are people not seeing?
zh: 人们没有看到的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you talk to an economist like Larry Summers who, on the OpenAI board with me, they'll talk about what is the value of technology?
zh: 如果你与一位像 Larry Summers 这样的经济学家交谈，他和我一起在 OpenAI 董事会，他们会谈论技术的价值是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Will it help strive productivity in the economy.
zh: 它会有助于推动经济中的生产力吗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at one of the big jumps in productivity in the economy was in the '90s, and I think a lot of folks I talked to think it was actually that very first wave of computing where people made ERP systems and just put accounting into computers and databases, even mainframes, we're talking like the PC era.
zh: 如果你观察经济中生产力的重大飞跃之一是在 90 年代，我认为与我交谈的许多人认为这实际上那是计算的第一波浪潮，人们制造了 ERP 系统，只是把会计放入计算机和数据库，甚至是大型机，我们谈论的是像 PC 时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it was such a huge step-up, just imagine the ledgers of numbers that you'd have for a large multinational company before and it truly just transformed departments.
zh: 因为它是如此巨大的一个提升，只要想象一下之前一家大型跨国公司拥有的数字账本，它真正地改变了部门。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you a little toy example.
zh: 我给你举个小玩具例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: My dad just retired.
zh: 我父亲刚退休。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was a mechanical engineer and he was talking about when he first started his career in the late '70s and he went into a mechanical engineering firm, the majority of the firm were drafts people.
zh: 他是一名机械工程师，他谈论起他在 70 年代后期刚开始职业生涯的时候，他进入一家机械工程公司，公司的绝大部分人都是制图人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, you take an engineering design but you needed to do all the different vantage points and for all the different floors and to give to the contractor to do the thing.
zh: 所以基本上，你拿一个工程设计，但你需要做所有的不同的视点，以及所有的不同的楼层，并交给承包商去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there are zero drafts people at his company.
zh: 现在，他的公司里零制图人员。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just make the design in first AutoCAD and now Revit and it's a 3D model and the drafting has actually been eliminated.
zh: 你只需要在 AutoCAD，现在的 Revit 中做设计，它是一个 3D 模型，制图实际上已经被消除了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not a thing one needs to do anymore.
zh: 这不再是一件需要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The actual design and drafting, drafting is not a thing that exists.
zh: 实际的设计和制图，制图不是一件存在的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a design.
zh: 它只是一个设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's true productivity gains, right?
zh: 那是真正的生产力收益，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the job of the mechanical engineering firm was to do a design.
zh: 这就像机械工程公司的工作是做一个设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: The drafting was this necessary output for the contractor, but it wasn't really adding value.
zh: 制图是承包商必须的必要产出，但它并没有真正增加价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just like the supply chain change.
zh: 它只是像供应链变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at the history of the software industry from the PC on, there's been meaningful productivity gains but just not nearly as meaningful as that first huge jump.
zh: 如果你观察从 PC 开始的软件行业历史，已经有有意义的生产力收益，但只是没有像第一次巨大飞跃那样有意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not smart enough to know exactly why, but it is interesting, the promise of productivity gains from technology hasn't been as realized I think as some people thought.
zh: 我不够聪明不知道确切原因，但这很有趣，技术带来的生产力收益的承诺并没有像一些人认为的那样被实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think agents will truly start to bend the curve again like we did in the very early days of computing because software is going from helping an individual be slightly more productive to actually accomplishing a job autonomously.
zh: 我认为智能体将真正开始再次改变曲线，就像我们在计算的早期做的那样，因为软件正在从帮助个人稍微提高生产力转变为真正自主地完成一项工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a consequence, just like you don't need drafts people in a mechanical engineering firm, you just won't need someone doing that thing anymore.
zh: 而且，正因如此，就像你在机械工程公司不需要制图人员一样，你只是不再需要有人做那件事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means they can do something else that's higher leverage and more productive and you can actually... A smaller group of people can accomplish more and truly drive productivity gains in the economy.
zh: 这意味着他们可以做其他更高杠杆率和更有生产力的事情，你实际上可以…… 更少的一群人可以完成更多的事情，并真正推动经济中的生产力收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you've ever sold enterprise software, you end up in these discussions as a vendor with the customer where you'll have a value discussion and you'll do these somewhat convoluted things like okay, it's like you're selling a sales thing.
zh: 我认为如果你曾经卖过企业软件，你最终会作为供应商与客户进行这些讨论，你会进行价值讨论，你会做这些有些复杂的事情，比如好吧，就像你在卖一个销售东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, well, if every salesperson sells 5% more... And you should pay us a million dollars.
zh: 好吧，如果每个销售人员多卖 5%…… 你应该付给我们一百万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's roughly that conversation and it's so unattributable especially... And it's why it's so hard to sell productivity software, which I learned the hard way, it's just hard to know what's the value of making everyone 10% more productive?
zh: 大致就是那个对话，而且它是如此难以归因，特别是…… 这就是为什么销售生产力软件如此困难，我通过艰难的方式学到了这一点，很难知道让每个人提高 10% 的生产力有什么价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you actually make them 10% more productive or did something else change?
zh: 你实际上让他们提高了 10% 的生产力了吗，还是其他什么改变了？

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't really know all these things.
zh: 你真的不知道所有这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now with an agent actually accomplishing a job, not only is it actually truly driving productivity in a very real way, but it's measurable as well.
zh: 但是现在，随着智能体实际完成一项工作，它不仅以非常真实的方式真正推动生产力，而且它也是可测量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all those things combined means I think this is actually a step change in how we think about software because it does a job autonomously, which is more self-evident, a productivity driver.
zh: 所以所有这些事情结合在一起意味着，我认为这是我们思考软件方式的真正一步式变化，因为它自主地做一项工作，这是更不言自明的生产力驱动因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's measurable so people value it differently as well, which is why I also believe in outcomes-based pricing for software.
zh: 它是可测量的，所以人们也以不同的方式评价它，这也是为什么我也相信软件的基于结果的定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of that combined to me, it feels like as significant as the cloud or I think more technologically, but just in terms of how it transforms the business model of the software industry where there's going to be a before and after.
zh: 所有这些结合在一起对我来说，感觉它就像云一样重要，或者我认为在技术上更重要，但就在它如何改变软件行业的商业模式方面，将会有一个之前和之后。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how many people still sell perpetually licensed on premises software, but it's de minimis at this point.
zh: 我不知道还有多少人销售永久许可的本地软件，但这已经是微不足道了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're going to go through a similar transition.
zh: 我认为我们将经历一个类似的转型。

speaker: Unknown
en: The whole market is going to go towards agents.
zh: 整个市场将走向智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the whole market is going to go towards outcomes-based pricing, not because it's the only way, but the market is going to pull everyone there because it's just so obviously the correct way to build and sell software.
zh: 我认为整个市场将走向基于结果的定价，不是因为它是唯一的方式，而是市场会将每个人拉到那里，因为它显然是构建和销售软件的正确方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me pull on that last thread.
zh: 让我拉扯这最后一条线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had Madhavan on the podcast recently, pricing expert, legend, monetizing innovation author and he talked about pricing strategy for AI companies and he was very much in your camp of, if you can, you need to price your product as an outcome-based product and the access uses exactly what you shared, which is, you can do that if you can attribute the impact and it's autonomous, it's running on its own.
zh: 所以我们最近请 Madhavan 上播客，定价专家，传奇人物，《Monetizing Innovation》作者，他谈到了 AI 公司的定价策略，他非常站在你的阵营，如果可以的话，你需要把你的产品定价为基于结果的产品，论据正好使用了你分享的，也就是，你可以这样做，如果你能归因影响并且它是自主的，它在独立运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he actually used Sierra as one of the shining examples of this being successful.
zh: 他实际上使用 Sierra 作为这方面成功的杰出例子之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just briefly just explain a little bit what is outcome-based pricing for people that haven't heard this term before and then just how does it work for Sierra to give an example?
zh: 你能简要解释一下什么是基于结果的定价,针对那些以前没听过这个词的人,然后再讲一下 Sierra 是怎么运作的,举个例子?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'll start with the example and then I'll broaden it.
zh: 好的,我先举例,然后再展开。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at Sierra, we help companies make customer facing AI agents primarily for customer service, but more broadly, for customer experience.
zh: 在 Sierra,我们帮助公司打造面向客户的 AI 智能体,主要是为了客户服务,但更广泛地说,是为了客户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you have a problem with your [inaudible 01:04:58], you'll call or chat with Harmony, who's their AI agent.
zh: 所以如果你的 [听不清 01:04:58] 有问题,你会打电话或与 Harmony 聊天,那是他们的 AI 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have ADT home security and your alarm doesn't work, you can chat with their AI agent.
zh: 如果你有 ADT 家庭安防系统且你的警报不工作,你可以与他们的 AI 智能体聊天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sonos speakers, a lot of different consumer brands.
zh: Sonos 音箱,很多不同的消费品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about running a call center, there's a cost for every phone call that you take.
zh: 如果你想一下运营呼叫中心,每一个电话都有成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of it is labor costs, but if you have, let's just say a typical phone call is anywhere between 10 and $20 USD.
zh: 大部分是劳动力成本,但假如说一个典型的电话在 10 到 20 美元之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of it's software, some of it's telephony, but a lot of it is just like the hourly wage of the person answering the phone.
zh: 有些是软件,有些是电话,但很多只是接电话的人的小时工资。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if an AI agent can take that call and solve it, that is in the industry often called a call deflection or a containment.
zh: 所以如果一个 AI 智能体能接那个电话并解决它,这在行业里通常被称为电话分流或遏制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that essentially means you saved, call it $15 because you didn't have to have someone pick up the phone.
zh: 这基本上意味着你省下了,比如 15 美元,因为你不必有人接电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in our industry, basically we say, "Hey, if the AI agent solves the customer's problem, they're happy with it and you didn't have to pick up the phone," there's a pre-negotiated rate for that and we call it resolution based.
zh: 所以在我们的行业,基本上我们会说,"嘿,如果 AI 智能体解决了客户的问题,他们很满意,而且你不必接电话,"这有一个预先协商的费率,我们称之为基于解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are other outcomes as well.
zh: 也有其他结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have some sales agents being paid a sales commission, believe it or not.
zh: 我们有一些销售智能体被支付销售佣金,信不信由你。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do.
zh: 我们确实有。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really think of our agents as truly customer experience like the concierge for your brand and we want to make sure that our business model is aligned with our customer's business model.
zh: 我们真的把我们的智能体视为真正的客户体验,像品牌的礼宾服务,我们要确保我们的商业模式与我们客户的商业模式一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you said, these agents need to be autonomous and the outcome has to be measurable.
zh: 如你所说,这些智能体需要是自主的,结果必须是可衡量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not always possible, but I think it's broadly possible.
zh: 这并不总是可能的,但我认为它是广泛可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's really neat about it is if you talk to any CFO or head of procurement with their big vendors, they look at the bill of materials and it's overwhelming and it's impossible to know if you're getting the value that you hoped from that contract.
zh: 真正有趣的是,如果你和任何 CFO 或采购主管谈他们的供应商,他们看物料清单,那是压倒性的,不可能知道你是否从那个合同中获得了你希望的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think consumption based, which was popular particularly in the infrastructure space is closer to it.
zh: 我认为基于消费,这在基础设施领域特别受欢迎,更接近它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm not sure a token is actually a good measure of value from AI either.
zh: 但我不确定 token 真的是衡量 AI 价值的好指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always use the analogy, like right now, most of the coding agents are priced per token or per utilization, but there's this famous story of an Apple engineer who had a bad manager who's like had you report how many lines of code you wrote every day?
zh: 我总是用这个类比,就像现在,大多数编码智能体是按 token 或按利用率定价的,但有一个著名的故事,一个苹果工程师有一个糟糕的经理,让他报告每天写了多少行代码?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which every engineer in the world knows is an idiotic way to measure productivity.
zh: 世界上每个工程师都知道这是衡量生产力的愚蠢方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: He famously went in with a report that had a negative number because I think he did a big refactoring, deleted a bunch and it was his way of saying like, fuck you to the man.
zh: 他著名地拿着一份有负数的报告进去,因为我认为他做了一个大的重构,删除了一堆,那是他表达 "去你的" 给老板的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think tokens are similar.
zh: 我认为 token 是类似的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you used a lot of tokens, like good for you, did it produce a pull request that was good?
zh: 是的,你用了很多 token,对你有好处,它是否产生了一个好的 pull request? [[626 ] 我认为这就是这一切的重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the whole point of all this.
zh: 我认为这就是所有这一切的重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a huge difference between outcomes-based pricing and usage based pricing because especially in AI, they're not necessarily even correlated and you could have a long phone call and not solve the customer's problem and they give you a negative review online and call the call center again, all that effort was for nothing.
zh: 我认为基于结果的定价和基于使用的定价有很大的区别,特别是在 AI 中,它们甚至不一定相关,你可能有一个很长的电话却没有解决客户的问题,他们在网上给你差评并再次呼叫呼叫中心,所有努力都是白费。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, you might've added negative value.
zh: 事实上,你可能增加了负价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, I am a huge believer in this.
zh: 所以,我对此非常相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's fun about it is it really just aligns... I think every technology company aspires to be a partner, not a vendor.
zh: 有趣的是它确实只是对齐... 我认为每家技术公司都渴望成为伙伴,而不是供应商。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think at Sierra, we are truly a partner to every single one of our customers because we're all aligned on what we want to achieve.
zh: 我认为在 Sierra,我们真的是每个客户伙伴,因为我们都对我们想要实现的目标达成一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is really where the software industry should go.
zh: 我认为这真的是软件行业应该去的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It requires a lot of different shape of a company.
zh: 它需要公司的很多不同形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to help your customers achieve those outcomes.
zh: 你必须能够帮助客户实现那些结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't just throw software at the wall because you'll never get paid if it doesn't.
zh: 你不能只是把软件扔在墙上,因为如果没有实现,你永远拿不到钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your orientation becomes so extremely customer-centric when you do this the right way.
zh: 当你以正确的方式做这件事时,你的导向变得极其以客户为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's just a better version of the software industry.
zh: 我认为这只是软件行业的更好版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's right from first principles, it's right for procurement partners and I think it's right for the world.
zh: 所以我认为从第一原理看它是正确的,对采购伙伴是正确的,我认为对世界也是正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been chatting a little bit about productivity gains.
zh: 我们聊了一点关于生产力提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of skepticism in the headlines these days of just like what is AI actually doing?
zh: 最近头条新闻里有很多关于 AI 到底在做什么的怀疑?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it actually helping people be more productive?
zh: 它真的在帮助人们提高生产力吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a recent study actually, I don't know if you saw, where they showed engineers were less productive with AI because it was just putting them in different directions.
zh: 最近有一项研究,我不知道你有没有看到,他们显示工程师有了 AI 反而生产力更低,因为它只是让他们指向不同的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: They had to research all what's going wrong here?
zh: 他们不得不研究这里出了什么问题?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think CX is a really good example where you clearly are seeing gains.
zh: 所以我认为 CX 是一个很好的例子,你在那里清楚地看到了收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you seeing actual gains at your company or any other company you work with outside of CX in terms of productivity that is like clearly yes, this is working and a huge deal?
zh: 在你的公司或你合作的 CX 以外的任何其他公司,你看到了真正的生产力收益吗,就是那种明确的 "是的,这很有效,而且是个大事"?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm extremely bullish on the productivity gains from AI, but I do think the tools and products right now are somewhat immature and it's quite counterintuitive.
zh: 我对 AI 带来的生产力收益极其看好,但我确实认为目前的工具和产品有些不成熟,而且非常反直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, almost every software engineering firm I know uses something like Cursor to help their software engineers.
zh: 所以,例如,我知道的几乎每家软件工程公司都使用像 Cursor 这样的东西来帮助他们的软件工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people use Cursor right now as a coding autocomplete, though they have a lot of agentic solutions and there's a lot of... OpenAI has Codex and Cloud has... I can't remember the Anthropic products.
zh: 现在大多数人把 Cursor 用作编码自动补全,尽管他们有很多智能体解决方案,而且有很多... OpenAI 有 Codex,Cloud 有... 我不记得 Anthropic 的产品了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's lots of agentic agents coming as well.
zh: 所以也有很多智能体即将到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the interesting things because the technology is immature, the code it produces often has problems.
zh: 其中一件有趣的事情是,因为技术还不成熟,它生成的代码经常有问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of people approaching this to actually realize those productivity gains because as any engineer who's written a lot of code will tell you, it's pretty easy to look at and edit and fix code you wrote.
zh: 很多人正在接近这个目标以真正实现那些生产力提升,因为正如任何写过大量代码的工程师会告诉你的,查看、编辑和修复你自己写的代码是很容易的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reviewing other people's code or particularly finding a subtle logical error in someone else's code is actually really hard.
zh: 审查别人的代码,或者特别是发现别人代码中微妙的逻辑错误,实际上是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually much harder than editing code that you wrote yourself.
zh: 这实际上比编辑你自己写的代码要难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if the code produced by a coding agent is often incorrect, it actually can take a lot of cognitive load and time to fix it.
zh: 所以如果编码智能体产生的代码经常是不正确的,修复它实际上会消耗大量的认知负荷和时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in fact, if you end up producing lots of issues with your customers, you could end up producing a lot of features, but actually, is like mucking up the machine a little bit and having something that's not ideal.
zh: 事实上,如果你最终给客户制造了很多问题,你可能会开发出很多功能,但实际上,这就像是在把机器搞得一团糟,并且产生了一些不理想的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a couple of techniques that I think are interesting.
zh: 我认为有几个有趣的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: First, I think there's a lot of AI starts now working on things like code reviews.
zh: 首先,我认为现在有很多 AI 初创公司正在从事代码审查之类的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this idea of self-reflection in agents is really important.
zh: 我认为智能体中这种自我反思的想法非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having AI supervise the AI is actually very effective.
zh: 让 AI 监督 AI 实际上是非常有效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just think about it this way, if you produce an AI agent that's right 90% of the time, that's not that great, but how hard would it be to make another AI agent to find the errors the other 10% of the time?
zh: 就这样想吧,如果你生成了一个 90% 时间都正确的 AI 智能体,那并不是很好,但是制造另一个 AI 智能体来找出另外 10% 时间内的错误会有多难呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: That might be a tractable problem.
zh: 这可能是一个可以解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that thing's right 90% of the time, just for argument's sake, you can wire those things together and have something that's right 99% of the time.
zh: 如果那个东西 90% 的时间都是正确的,只是为了讨论起见,你可以把这些东西连接在一起,得到一个 99% 时间都正确的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's just a math problem and it turns out that you can make something to generate code, you can make something to review code and you're essentially using compute for cognitive capacity and you can layer on more layers of cognition and thinking and reasoning and produce things increasingly robust.
zh: 所以这只是一个数学问题,事实证明你可以制造某种东西来生成代码,你可以制造某种东西来审查代码,而且你本质上是使用计算来换取认知能力,你可以分层叠加更多的认知层、思考层和推理层,并生成越来越健壮的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm very excited about that.
zh: 所以我对这一点感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing though is root cause analysis.
zh: 另一件事是根本原因分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have an engineer at Sierra who exclusively focuses on the model context protocol server serving our cursor instance.
zh: 所以我们在 Sierra 有一位工程师,专门专注于服务于我们 cursor 实例的模型上下文协议服务器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our whole philosophy is, if cursor generated something incorrect, rather than just fixing it, try to root cause it.
zh: 我们的整个哲学是,如果 cursor 生成了不正确的东西,而不是仅仅修复它,而是尝试找到根本原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try to get it so the next time Cursor will produce the correct code and essentially, is context engineering.
zh: 试图让下一次 Cursor 能够生成正确的代码,本质上,这就是上下文工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: What context did Cursor not have that would've been necessary to produce the right outcome?
zh: Cursor 缺少什么上下文本来是产生正确结果所必需的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think people who are trying to get productivity gains in departments like software engineering need to stop waiting for the models to magically work if they want to see the gains now.
zh: 所以我认为那些试图在软件工程等部门获得生产力提升的人需要停止等待模型神奇地工作,如果他们现在就想看到收益的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you really have to create root cause analysis and systems and say, how do we go root cause every bad line of code and actually give the right context and produce the right system so the models can do it today?
zh: 你真的必须建立根本原因分析和系统,并说,我们如何对每一行糟糕的代码进行根本原因分析,并实际上提供正确的上下文并生成正确的系统,以便模型今天就能做到?

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time that'll probably be less necessary and you'll have less context engineering necessary to do it, but you really have to think of this as a system and I think people are waiting for the models to just magically get better.
zh: 随着时间的推移,这可能就不那么有必要了,你将需要更少的上下文工程来做这件事,但你真的必须把它看作一个系统,我认为人们正在等待模型只是神奇地变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, well that will happen eventually, but if you want the gains now you got to put in the work.
zh: 而我会说,嗯,那最终会发生,但如果你现在想要收益,你就必须投入工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's essentially why applied AI companies exist.
zh: 这本质上就是应用 AI 公司存在的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the work is non-trivial, but you can do it.
zh: 这项工作并非微不足道,但你可以做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, for customers using platforms like Sierra, yeah, AI agents aren't perfect, but we're creating a system that lets customers create a virtuous cycle of improvement.
zh: 因此,对于使用像 Sierra 这样平台的客户来说,是的,AI 智能体并不完美,但我们正在创建一个系统,让客户能够创建一个改进的良性循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to go from a 65% automated resolution rate to 75%, we have a billion tools to let AI help you do that, identify opportunities for improvement, figure out why people are frustrated, what new capabilities can we add to our agent to improve the resolution rate?
zh: 如果你想从 65% 的自动化解决率提高到 75%,我们有十亿种工具让 AI 帮助你做到这一点,识别改进机会,弄清楚人们为什么会感到沮丧,我们可以给我们的智能体添加什么新能力来提高解决率?

speaker: Unknown
en: And you let AI put the needles at the top of the haystack on your behalf and I think that's really the way to optimize these systems.
zh: 你让 AI 代表你把针放在干草堆的顶端,我认为这确实是优化这些系统的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never heard of this technique of improving Cursor by adding additional context.
zh: 我从未听说过这种通过添加额外上下文来改进 Cursor 的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the actual way of doing that?
zh: 实际的做法是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You build an MCP server that everything runs through or is it like you add Cursor rules?
zh: 你构建一个 MCP 服务器让所有东西都通过它运行,还是说你添加 Cursor 规则?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the actual approach there?
zh: 实际的方法是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm probably out of my depth here, but it's essentially MCP because that's how you provide context to Cursor.
zh: 我可能有点超出我的深度了,但这本质上是 MCP,因为那是你向 Cursor 提供上下文的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that almost always when you have a model making a poor decision, if it's a good model, it's lack of context.
zh: 我认为几乎总是当你有一个模型做出了糟糕的决定时,如果它是一个好模型,那就是缺乏上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you really want to find the intersection of your particular product and code base with the context available to these coding agents and systems and fix it at the root is the principle here.
zh: 所以,你真的想要找到你的特定产品和代码库与这些编码智能体和系统可用的上下文之间的交集,并在根本上解决它,这就是这里的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got it.
zh: 明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is very cool.
zh: 那非常酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hadn't heard of people doing that, model context protocol, makes sense.
zh: 我以前没听说过人们这样做,模型上下文协议,有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've talked about productivity gains outside TX.
zh: 我们已经讨论了 TX 之外的生产力提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to give you a chance to share how amazing what you've built is, what are some of the gains you see from people using Sierra?
zh: 为了给你一个机会分享你构建的东西有多棒,你看到使用 Sierra 的人有哪些收益?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, our customers see anywhere between 50 and 90% of their customer service interactions completely automated, which I think is really exciting.
zh: 是的,我们的客户看到他们 50% 到 90% 的客户服务互动完全自动化,我认为这真的很令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we serve just a really, really broad range of customers.
zh: 我们服务非常非常广泛的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: We serve the health insurance industry, the healthcare provider space, banks.
zh: 我们服务于医疗保险行业、医疗保健提供领域、银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can actually refinance your home using an agent.
zh: 你实际上可以使用智能体来为你的房屋再融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of our customers built on our platform to the telecommunications industry, DIRECTV, SiriusXM to a lot of retailers as well, which is really fun.
zh: 我们的一个客户在我们的平台上构建了服务于电信行业、DIRECTV、SiriusXM 以及许多零售商的应用,这真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone from Wayfair to clothing retailers like OluKai and Chubbies Shorts.
zh: 从 Wayfair 到像 OluKai 和 Chubbies Shorts 这样的服装零售商。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's really neat about it is it's a pretty diverse range of use cases and it's everything from helping you sign up for... We have an agent that helps with customer support in one of the big dating applications to helping you upgrade or downgrade your SiriusXM plan.
zh: 真正很酷的是,它的用例范围非常多样,从帮助您注册……我们有一个智能体在其中一个大型约会应用程序中帮助客户支持,到帮助您升级或降级您的 SiriusXM 计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, it's really funny, we do technical support from everything from home alarm systems to sonar speakers to more recently, CAT scan machines, which I think is amazing.
zh: 实际上,这真的很有趣,我们做技术支持,从家庭报警系统到声纳音箱,到最近的 CAT 扫描机器,我认为这太神奇了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So technicians going in and fixing the CAT scan machine can chat with an AI agent to help them guide them through that process.
zh: 所以进去修复 CAT 扫描机器的技术人员可以与 AI 智能体聊天,以帮助他们引导他们完成该过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're the leader in the space, we're trying to enable every company in the world to create their agent with their brand at the top that I think will become as meaningful of a digital touch point as their website or their mobile app.
zh: 我们是该领域的领导者，我们正在尝试让世界上的每一家公司都能创建他们的智能体，并在顶端加上他们的品牌，我认为这将成为像他们的网站或移动应用一样有意义的数字接触点。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the short term, it can really transform the costs of running a customer service team.
zh: 在短期内，它确实可以改变运营客户服务团队的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's remarkable is do so with really high customer satisfaction scores.
zh: 而且值得注意的是，做到这一点的同时还能获得非常高的客户满意度分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: That Weight Watchers agent, I believe has a customer satisfaction score of 4.6 out of five, which is pretty amazing.
zh: 那个 Weight Watchers 智能体，我相信它的客户满意度分数是 4.6 分（满分 5 分），这非常惊人。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而服务领域有趣的一点在于，通常是人们遇到了问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, when you have a clear, I don't know if you use them in the airport, I think that agent has a CSAT score of 4.7 out of five people are coming in with a problem and [inaudible 01:16:19] delighted.
zh: 所以，当你有一个清晰的，我不知道你是否在机场用过它们，我认为那个智能体的 CSAT 分数是 4.7 分（满分 5 分），人们带着问题进来，然后[听不清 01:16:19]感到高兴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's really the opportunity here.
zh: 我认为这确实是这里的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our whole vision is that we're going to move towards a world where every single one of the interactions with your customers can be instant.
zh: 我们的整个愿景是，我们将迈向一个世界，在这个世界里，与客户的每一次互动都可以是即时的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be multilingual, it can be over audio, it can be over chat, it can be digital, it can be over the phone and it can be very personalized.

speaker: Unknown
